gaps.why_now: The existing Phase 9 build step is the narrowest honest place to make the trace-events lane reviewable without pretending the runtime sample already exists.
A dedicated survey gate records the roadmap anchor, current repo gap, and remaining bounded next steps before the first runtime trace-events starter lands.
The next meaningful product step is a small sample-backed lifecycle starter that models descriptor metadata and a narrow event catalog instead of jumping straight to a broad runtime implementation.
A dedicated Phase 9 module test should land alongside the first starter sample so lifecycle and event-name expectations stay bounded and reviewable.

The Linux sample and its ftrace selftests already point to a small named event family, so the survey note should preserve that scope for the eventual starter instead of leaving the lane underspecified.
A loadable trace-events module, registration hooks, and lifecycle parity still depend on runtime substrate pieces that the repo has not started yet.
